title: Love is different
takeaway: Love follows its own rules. Its rewards and its pains are like nothing else.
scene: Every couplet in this ghazal ends with the word 'vakhri', which means 'different' or 'one of a kind'. The poet lists all the ways love doesn't work like anything else.

original: اوہدا ناز نخرا ادا وکھری اے
جو موہندی دلاں نوں حیا وکھری اے
transliteration: Ohda naaz nakhra ada vakhri ae
Jo mohndi dilaan nu, hayaa vakhri ae
translation: The beloved's charm, playfulness and style are one of a kind;
the modesty that wins hearts is one of a kind.
couplets.story: The Beloved's charm and way of being are unlike anyone else's. Even their shyness is special, and it steals people's hearts.

original: اساں دل سی منگیا اوہنے توڑ دتا
لگا روگ وکھرا، دوا وکھری اے
transliteration: Asaan dil si mangiya, ohne tor ditta
Laga rog vakhra, dawa vakhri ae
translation: I asked for a heart, and they broke mine.
This illness is different, and so is its cure.
couplets.story: He asked for the Beloved's heart, and got his own broken instead. Love is a strange illness, and its medicine is just as strange.

original: تڑپ دل نوں دتی جگر ساڑ دتا
محبت دی ویکھو جزاء وکھری اے
transliteration: Tarap dil nu ditti, jigar saar ditta
Mohabbat di vekho jazaa vakhri ae
translation: It gave my heart restlessness and burned me inside.
Look: love's reward is different.
couplets.story: Love made his heart restless and burned him up inside. Most things reward you with comfort. Love rewards you with this, and somehow he still wants it.

original: سدا لٹکے رہندے نیں پلکاں تے موتی
یاراں دی یارو عطا وکھری اے
transliteration: Sada latke rehnde nain palkaan te moti
Yaaraan di yaaro ataa vakhri ae
translation: Pearls always hang on my eyelashes.
Friends, the Beloved's gifts are different.
couplets.story: There are always 'pearls', tears, hanging on his eyelashes. The Beloved's presents aren't like anyone else's.

original: کہدے پیر پائیاں ایہہ پھیلی اے خشبو
کہ سارے چمن دی فضا وکھری اے
transliteration: Kihde pair paaiyaan eh phaili ae khushboo
Ke saare chaman di fazaa vakhri ae
translation: Whose feet have passed this way, that such a fragrance has spread,
and the air of the whole garden feels different?
couplets.story: Someone must have walked through here. A wonderful scent has filled the air, and the whole garden suddenly feels different.

original: عشقے دے لانبو دا ہے ساڑ وکھرا
وچھوڑے دی ہوندی سزا وکھری اے
transliteration: Ishqe de laambu da hai saar vakhra
Vichhore di hondi sazaa vakhri ae
translation: The burn of love's flames is different;
the punishment of separation is different.
couplets.story: Love's fire burns in its own way. Being apart from someone you love is a punishment like no other.

original: کدی ٹھارے سینہ کدی ساڑ سٹے
محبت رسم تے جفا وکھری اے
transliteration: Kadi thaare seena, kadi saar sutte
Mohabbat rasm te jafaa vakhri ae
translation: Sometimes it cools the chest, sometimes it burns it to ash.
Love's customs, and its cruelty, are different.
couplets.story: One minute love calms you down, the next it sets you on fire. It follows its own rules, even when it hurts you.

original: میں تارو عشق دے سمندر چ ڈگا
میرے عشق دی انتہا وکھری اے
transliteration: Main taaroo ishq de samundar ch digga
Mere ishq di intehaa vakhri ae
translation: I'm a swimmer who fell into the ocean of love;
how far my love goes is different.
couplets.story: He's like a swimmer who fell into an ocean of love. No one can measure how deep his love goes.

original: ذکر چھوہ کے حوراں دا پرچاوے ملاں
میرے دل دی چاہت صدا وکھری اے
transliteration: Zikr chhoh ke hooraan da parchaave mullaan
Mere dil di chaahat sadaa vakhri ae
translation: The mullah tries to win me over by talking about the maidens of paradise,
but my heart's desire has always been different.
couplets.story: The preacher tries to tempt him with talk of paradise and its rewards. It doesn't work. What his heart wants has always been something else.

original: میں ویکھاں صنم تے خدا یاد آوے
نرالے حسن دی ضیا وکھری اے
transliteration: Main vekhaan sanam te Khuda yaad aave
Niraale husn di ziyaa vakhri ae
translation: When I look at the beloved, I remember God.
The light of this rare beauty is different.
couplets.story: This is the key line. When he looks at the beautiful Beloved, it makes him think of God. Their beauty has a light unlike any other.

original: احمدؔ سب دا درد دی محبت دا بھکھا
طبیعت بنائی خدا وکھری اے
transliteration: Ahmad sab da dardi, mohabbat da bhukkha
Tabiyat banaai Khuda vakhri ae
translation: Ahmad feels everyone's pain and is hungry for love:
God made his nature different.
couplets.story: He ends by describing himself. He feels everyone's pain, and all he wants is love. God simply made him that way.

deeper:
Two couplets make this poem's spiritual meaning plain. The mullah tempts him with the maidens of paradise, but 'my heart's desire has always been different': he wants God Himself, not His rewards. And 'when I look at the beloved, I remember God' is the Sufi idea that all earthly beauty is a reflection of God's beauty. Seeing it rightly leads the heart back to Him.

The last couplet gives a portrait of the poet as a man who carries everyone's pain. That fits what his friend wrote about him at the start of the book.
why: The repeated word 'different' makes it a simple poem to follow, and it builds to one beautiful line: seeing beauty and remembering God.
prompt: When you see something beautiful, in nature, in a person or in art, what does it make you think of?
notes: Printed in two columns; the right-hand column is the first line of each couplet.
